# Changelog 

## Amni-Learn v5.68.0 — Kokoro voice: buzzing GPU output auto-detected, falls to CPU cleanly - 2026-07-10
- Anthony's device ear check caught the Kokoro tier **buzzing instead of speaking** — a known WebGPU failure where some GPU/driver combos (notably AMD on Windows) compute the neural vocoder wrong and emit static. The plumbing was fine; the GPU output was numerical garbage.
- **Warm-up quality gate**: `_kkAudioOk()` now inspects the actual warm-up waveform — NaN anywhere, >15% clipped samples, or no quiet frames (real speech always has silence gaps; continuous buzz has none) flags the tier as garbage.
- **Tier ladder**: WebGPU fp32 → on garbage or failure, the GPU session is disposed and Kokoro retries on **CPU (WASM, q8 ~92MB)** — same natural voice, slower synth but correct — then Piper HD, then Web Speech. Manual overrides: localStorage `amni-learn-kk-device`='wasm' (skip GPU, works even on non-WebGPU devices) or 'webgpu' (force GPU only); `amni-learn-kk`='off' still kills the whole tier.
- Verified headless in three modes: clean-GPU (single webgpu init, all speech through Kokoro), garbage-GPU (buzz waveform at warm-up → disposed → q8/wasm init → phonics tiles + storybook autoplay all through CPU Kokoro, zero Piper calls), and kokoro-404 (Piper still carries both modules). Zero page errors everywhere. SW cache v1266→v1267. Re-check on device: reload the page once, reopen Storybook — first CPU run downloads the q8 model (~92MB) with the progress banner.

## Amni-Calc v5.67.0 — NEW MODULE: Hydraulics / Fluid Power - 2026-07-10
- **Brand-new sidebar module** between Pumps and Thermal — the suite finally speaks fluid power. Three cards plus a live cylinder schematic:
- **⚡ CYLINDER DESIGNER**: force + push/pull + system pressure + stroke + mounting + target speed → **the bore and rod to buy** off the ISO 3320 / ISO 4395 standard series. Pushing rods are sized by real Euler buckling (P_cr = π²EI/(KL)² with published end-condition K factors, industry-standard FoS 3.5 over the stroke); pulled rods by tension. Force uses P·A with a stated 0.9 mechanical-hydraulic efficiency; pull sizing correctly works on the annulus. Honest verdicts when the stroke demands a rod beyond 180 mm (shorten, guide the mounting, or go telescopic) or the force exceeds a 250 bore (raise pressure or split cylinders). Reports both-direction forces, achieved buckling FoS, the flow your target speed needs, hydraulic power, and the area ratio — with a pressure-intensification warning for rod-side meter-out. APPLY floods the analysis card.
- **CYLINDER ANALYSIS**: bore + rod + P + flow → extend/retract force and speed, areas, φ, power — and a schematic drawn to your proportions.
- **ACCUMULATOR SIZING**: usable ΔV + P_min/P_max + isothermal-or-adiabatic → gas volume by the catalog gas-law method in absolute pressures, precharge at 90% of P_min. Rapid discharge honestly needs the bigger shell (n = 1.4).
- Tests: new hydraulics_audit.js (22 hand anchors incl. proofs that the next-smaller bore and rod each FAIL — the picks are minimal, not just sufficient) — all 9 suites green, 295 anchors. Cache-busters fixes?v=eng12, engineer?v=eng13. 17 modules now open design-first.

## Amni-Learn v5.66.0 — Kokoro natural voice: a genuinely human-sounding narrator - 2026-07-10
- **New top voice tier**: Kokoro-82M (Apache-2.0, the consensus best small neural TTS) now powers Phonics and Storybook narration on WebGPU-capable devices — near-human prosody and warmth vs Piper's flat cadence. Runs 100% in-browser (transformers.js/ONNX, `af_heart` voice); nothing ever leaves the device, same privacy story as before.
- **Tiering, fail-closed**: WebGPU devices → Kokoro (fp32); anything else or any load/generate failure → the existing Piper HD voice, then Web Speech — zero regression paths. Kill switch: localStorage `amni-learn-kk`='off'. Model (~326MB) downloads once on first module open with the existing progress banner, then persists in the browser's transformers cache; the JS bundle + ONNX runtime (34MB) are vendored same-origin under `learn/vendor/kokoro/` so the service worker caches them like the Piper assets.
- **Shared synth core**: `_synthWav()` now feeds both the phonics speech path and the storybook page reader (word-by-word highlight + autoplay untouched); storybook reads at a gentle 0.95 speed.
- Verified headless: real bundle import smoke test (KokoroTTS/TextSplitterStream/env exports present), mocked end-to-end probe — phonics warm-on-open fires Kokoro with correct model/dtype/device, tile taps and storybook pages generate through Kokoro with autoplay advancing, zero Piper calls, zero page errors — plus a 404-fallback probe proving the Piper path still carries both modules when Kokoro is unavailable. SW cache v1265→v1266. Device ear check pending (headless is silent).

## Amni-Calc v5.65.0 — DESIGNER batch 3: pipes & motors close out the rollout - 2026-07-10
- **⚡ PIPE DESIGNER (Fluids)**: flow + run length + pressure-drop budget + fluid + pipe material + service → the Schedule 40 pipe size to buy. Walks the published ASME B36.10 bore ladder (½"–12", PVC Sch 40 and stainless 40S share these dimensions), Swamee-Jain friction with exact 64/Re laminar handling, and standard-practice velocity caps per service (pump suction 1.5 m/s to protect NPSH, discharge/general 3, gravity 1.2, gas 20) — both criteria shrink with diameter so the smallest passing size is the unique right answer. Reports velocity, Reynolds regime, friction factor, actual ΔP vs budget and head loss; if nothing ≤12" passes it says so with the DN300 numbers and what to change. APPLY floods the Moody card.
- **⚡ MOTOR DESIGNER (Motors)**: load torque + speed + load type + supply Hz + sizing margin → the motor to buy: required kW from P = Tω exactly, IEC kW and NEMA HP picks off the standard ladders, pole count (smallest synchronous speed above your rpm, with an honest "direct drive is impossible — VFD or gearbox" verdict above the 2-pole ceiling), NEMA design letter from load type (B general / C loaded starts / D punch-hoist), estimated full-load speed from the design's slip, full-load torque check against your load, and an FLA estimate. APPLY floods all six analysis cards — torque, FLA, service factor, sync/slip, NEMA frame lookup and the torque-speed curve.
- That completes the design-first rollout: **16 modules now open with a START HERE card**. Tests: new designer_batch3_audit.js (32 hand-computed anchors incl. the DN65-discharge/DN100-suction velocity gate and 50 Hz pole picks) — all 8 suites green, 273 anchors total. Cache-busters fixes?v=eng11, engineer?v=eng12.

## Amni-Calc v5.59.0 — DESIGNER cards across the suite + service conditions - 2026-07-10
- **Eight modules now open with a ⚡ DESIGNER — START HERE card** that speaks the engineer's question, not the calculator's: springs (force + deflection → wire Ø, coil Ø, turns, free length — five wire materials with Shigley A/d^m strengths, auto-picked from temperature/environment), shafts (torque + material → stock diameter, strength AND 0.25°/m stiffness governed), bearings (load + speed + life target → required C, ball & roller), welds (load + length → fillet leg), NEC wire (load + run + max drop → smallest AWG passing ampacity and drop together), battery (target V + Ah → S×P topology), vibration isolators (mass + disturbing Hz + isolation % → mount stiffness, per-mount, static deflection sanity). Every designer rounds to real stock sizes, gives explicit "nothing passes — here's what to change" verdicts, and has APPLY → to populate the module's full analysis.
- **Service conditions on bolts & springs** (loading static/vibration/shock · service temperature · dry/wet/marine/chemical): vibration on bolts raises preload to 90% proof, demands thread locking, and adds a Goodman fatigue factor using published Se (8.8 = 129, 10.9 = 162, 12.9 = 190, SAE 5/7/8 MPa — grades without published data say so instead of guessing); shock tightens all criteria; temperature triggers standards-based warnings (>150 °C ISO 898 envelope, >300 °C → A193 B7); wet/marine/chemical recommend A2-70 / A4-80 with galvanic notes. Springs gate materials by real temperature limits and pick 302 SS for corrosive service. Static ideal state = just leave the defaults.
- Tests: designer_suite_audit.js (19 anchors: shaft 19.4→20 mm, bearing C 60.8 kN, weld 2.44→3 mm, isolator ≈323 kN/m, wire #6 @ 30 A/100 ft/3%, spring fixed-point convergence, bolt Goodman n_f) — all 5 suites green. Cache-busters fixes?v=eng9, overrides?v=eng3, engineer?v=eng10.

## Amni-Calc v5.57.0 — BOLT DESIGNER: think like an engineer, not a calculator - 2026-07-10
- New **⚡ BOLT DESIGNER — START HERE** card leads the Bolts module, matching how the problem actually arrives: **how many + what material + what load → what size, what torque, what preload, what to expect.** It walks the 81-size catalog (optionally restricted to a thread family), finds the smallest bolt meeting proof-usage ≤ 90%, separation ≥ 1.5× and tension-shear interaction < 1, then quotes: the size, the wrench torque (N·m and lbf·ft), per-bolt preload, margins, minimum thread engagement in steel AND aluminum, plus the next size up as a conservative alternative.
- **APPLY TO FULL ANALYSIS →** loads the recommendation into the joint card — torque sequence, tightening pattern, and stripping check all light up with the same numbers. Reusable (75% proof) vs permanent (90%) service selector; clear "no size passes" verdict instead of silent oversizing.
- Boundary-anchored tests: 4 × SAE-5 carrying 20 kN picks M6 because M5 misses proof usage at 90.04% (bolts_designer_audit.js, 9 assertions). Cache-busters calc-fixes.js?v=eng8, calc-engineer.js?v=eng9.

## Amni-Calc v5.56.0 — AGMA pitting + thread stripping - 2026-07-10
- **AGMA pitting (surface durability)** in Gears: σ_H = Z_E·√(W_t·K_o·K_v·K_H/(d_p·b·Z_I)) with spur geometry factor Z_I from φ and m_G, Grade-1 allowable S_c = 2.22·HB+200, and a pitting safety factor with status. Gears previously had only Lewis bending — pitting usually governs hardened industrial gears.
- **Thread engagement / stripping** in Bolts: basic-size FED-STD-H28 shear areas (A_ext = 0.75π·K_n·L_e, A_int = 0.875π·d·L_e), strip forces both sides at 0.6·S_u, governing failure mode, and the minimum engagement for break-before-strip. Bolt size and S_u follow the joint card automatically; the old "1.0·d steel / 1.5·d aluminum" note is now a real calculation. Tests: gaps2_audit.js grows to 21 (Z_I ≈ 0.1286 anchor, M12 minor-dia/area/L_e-min checks); all suites green. Cache-buster calc-fixes.js?v=eng7.

## Amni-Calc v5.55.0 — Tolerance stack-up, natural convection, fouled U - 2026-07-10
- **Tolerance stack-up (WC / RSS)** in Fits & Tol: build a ± dimension chain (add/remove rows, +/− direction), get the nominal gap, worst-case limits, RSS ±3σ limits, and the top contributor to variance — with an interference warning when the worst case goes negative.
- **Natural convection (Churchill-Chu)** in Thermal: vertical-plate and horizontal-cylinder correlations across all Ra, air properties auto-interpolated at film temperature (Incropera A.4) or fully manual for other fluids; computed h auto-fills the Convection card. Closes the free-convection gap (Dittus-Boelter only covered forced flow). Textbook anchor verified: 0.5 m plate, 60→20 °C → h ≈ 4.9 W/m²K.
- **Fouled U (TEMA)** in Heat Exchangers: pick hot/cold-side service from typical TEMA fouling resistances (or custom), get U_dirty, % derate and extra-area requirement — written into the LMTD card so Q reflects end-of-service. Tests: gaps2_audit.js (13) + all suites green. Cache-buster calc-fixes.js?v=eng6.

## Amni-Calc v5.54.0 — NEW MODULE: Fits & Tolerances (ISO 286) + press-fit design + beam modes - 2026-07-10
- **Fits & Tolerances** (new Mechanical tab): nominal Ø + hole/shaft class → exact ISO 286 limits, clearances/interference, fit classification, and a tolerance-zone diagram. Preferred-fits dropdown (H11/c11 loose running → H7/s6 medium drive) or fully custom letter+grade (holes D–H, JS; shafts c–s incl. split subranges for c/r/s; IT5–IT11 to Ø500, published table values, spot-verified: 25 H7 = +21/0, g6 = −7/−20, p6 = +35/+22). Sizes where the standard's subranges aren't covered say so explicitly instead of extrapolating.
- **Press / shrink fit (Lamé)**: diametral interference (auto-filled min/max from an interference or transition fit above) → contact pressure, holding torque and axial capacity at BOTH interference extremes, hub-bore tangential stress, and hub heating ΔT for thermal assembly. Closed-form verified: Ø50/Ø100 steel, 0.05 mm → 75.0 MPa exactly.
- **Beam natural frequencies** (new card in Vibration): first 3 modes for simply-supported / cantilever / fixed-fixed / fixed-pinned uniform beams (Blevins λ² constants), with critical rpm — the module previously only handled SDOF systems.
- Goal-seek works on the new module for free — including SOLVE FOR over the preferred-fits dropdown ("which standard fit gives me ≥20 µm clearance?"). Tests: calc/tests/fits_audit.js (23 assertions) + all prior suites green. Cache-busters calc-fixes.js?v=eng5, calc-engineer.js?v=eng8.

## Amni-Learn v5.45.0 — Module /loop iter 1: tracing actually teaches tracing - 2026-07-10
- **Tracing scribble-pass fixed**: the checker only measured how much of the letter got covered (32-45%), with no penalty for ink outside it — any big scribble passed. Now dual-gate: letter coverage (45% L1 / 55% L2+) AND precision — the share of drawn ink that lands on the letter or a small halo around it (55% L1 / 68% L2+, halo = letter re-stroked at max(36, fontSize×0.12)px so honest edge-overshoot still counts).
- **Teaching feedback**: empty canvas → "Trace the letter first! ✏️"; low coverage → "Cover the whole letter — trace every part!"; low precision → "Oops — stay on the letter, not outside it!" — tells the child what to fix instead of a generic "Keep Trying".
- Test hook `window.__traceT` (cov/prec/ink) gated by sessionStorage `trace-test`. Verified headless: scribble = 100% coverage but 18.9% precision → rejected; 206-point on-glyph trace → cov 1.0 prec 1.0 → passes; empty → prompt. Zero page errors. SW cache v1256→v1257.

- Seals module rebalanced like springs/bolts: MATERIAL PROPERTIES moved under the gland config (it's a selection aid) — columns now 3/3 instead of 2-vs-5.
- Sidebar auto-scrolls the active module into view (on load-restore and every tab click) — the current tab was off-screen in the 30+ list whenever you worked low in a category.
- ⌖ SOLVE FOR panels refresh their TARGET OUTPUT list every time they reopen — previously a panel opened once cached its outputs, so switching spring type (or any mode dropdown) left it aiming at stale result labels. Cache-buster calc-engineer.js?v=eng3.

## Amni-Calc v5.43.0 — Goal-seek over dropdowns + sticky quick-nav + uniform card rhythm - 2026-07-10
- **⌖ SOLVE FOR now handles dropdowns** (marked ▾ in the BY VARYING list): every option is swept — inline onchange side-effects honored so coating→K style pickers work — and the option whose output lands closest to the target wins, with a "(nearest available — no exact match)" tag when the discrete catalog can't hit it exactly. Ask "which bolt SIZE gives me 25 kN preload" or "which bearing type hits 40 000 h" directly. Unit selectors are excluded (changing display units isn't a design variable).

- **Consistent card rhythm**: one uniform gap between all cards in every module — the mix of inline margin-tops (static 1rem, injected 0.6rem, none) is normalized away. Cache-buster calc-engineer.js?v=eng2.

## Amni-Calc v5.42.0 — Springs/Belleville packs, bolts fine threads, flicker-free results - 2026-07-10
- **Belleville springs rebuilt on real physics**: found and fixed a wrong Almen-Laszlo implementation (`ratio·(ratio−0.5)·ratio` went NEGATIVE for DIN A-series discs with h₀/t<0.5) — replaced with the standard `F(s)=C·t³·s·[(h₀−s)(h₀−s/2)/t²+1]`, plus real disc inputs (D_e, D_i, t, h₀ — previously D_i was hardcoded 0.51·D_e and preset dims were silently ignored), numeric peak detection for snap-through discs, and bisection deflection solve. Node-verified against catalog magnitudes.
- **STACK / PACK BUILDER**: single / series-alternating / parallel-nested / series-parallel packs (n_s × n_p) with k_eq, stack deflection (nonlinear per-disc for belleville), free stack height L₀ = n_s(h₀+n_p·t), solid height, and force capacity.
- **PACK VIEW**: new 2D cross-section canvas showing the actual parts and orientations — belleville discs alternate ⟨⟩ in series and nest for parallel; helical springs draw end-to-end / side-by-side. The 3D view now builds the same arrangement (cone washers with real flip orientation, extension hooks, series seat plates, die springs in steel grey) instead of one generic helix for all five types.
- **Presets doubled**: 19 belleville entries (DIN 2093 A/B/C series + M-bolt washer sizes, forces computed from the corrected formula), plus new compression/extension/torsion/die entries (valve spring, tailgate assist, clothespin, ISO die extremes...). Loading a belleville preset now fills the real disc dimensions.
- **De-duplicated the springs tab**: the old injected Belleville card was silently hijacking the calculation with a cruder linear model (`hookSpringType` rerouted calcSpring) — removed along with three other superseded injected cards; the rect-wire DIE SPRING card (ISO 10243) stays, now with its own output area.
- **Bolts**: thread sizes grouped by family (METRIC COARSE / METRIC FINE / INCH UNC / INCH UNF) sorted by diameter — the 19 fine-thread sizes were buried unsorted at the bottom of an 81-item flat list. Pattern & torque-sequence cards now prepopulate from the joint analysis (bolt count auto-syncs and re-renders the star sequence; torque card was already synced). Pattern/grade-notes cards moved under the config column; torque card stays with results.
- **Flicker fix**: new `__morphRes` differ — identical recomputes are zero-DOM-write no-ops, value changes patch text in place instead of rebuilding the panel (engineer-unit-layer aware: converted displays don't flip back to SI). Applied to setRes, setCardOut, bolt joint, spring results and stack readouts.
- **Layout**: springs and bolts columns rebalanced — inputs/presets/stack-builder left, results/visuals right (was 1 card vs 5).
- Tests: new `calc/tests/spring_stack_audit.js` (20 assertions: corrected flat-load positivity, catalog values, peak detection, stack math, degressive inverse) + engineer_layer (74) + unit_audit (61) all green. Cache-busters `?v=eng2`. Backups `backups/amni-calc-deployed/*.v5.42.0.bak`.

## Amni-Calc v5.40.0 — Engineer Refresh: output units, goal seek, module search - 2026-07-10
- New additive layer `calc/calc-engineer.js` (loaded last, DOM-only — obfuscated app and audited math untouched):
  - **Results follow YOUR units**: every numeric result value (stress, force, torque, flow, power, temperature, inertia, section modulus...) now converts with the sidebar SI/US toggle, and clicking any result value cycles it through that dimension's units (choice persists per dimension). Exact UCORE-grade factors; Δ-temperature values are protected from absolute-offset conversion; psi/lbf auto-step up to ksi/kip when large.
  - **⌖ SOLVE FOR (goal seek) on every compute card**: pick any output, enter the value you need (in the displayed unit), choose which input to vary — a secant solver with bracketed-bisection fallback finds the input, respecting display quantization; the input is restored on failure. Turns every one of the ~39 one-way calculators into an inverse designer (required section for a target deflection, preload for a target torque, pipe size for a target head loss...).
  - **Sidebar module search** ("/" to focus, Enter opens the first hit): filters the 30+ tabs by name AND by every card title/input label inside each module, so "torque" finds Bolts, Shafts, and Motors; empty categories collapse.
  - **Quick-nav chips** at the top of every multi-card module jump straight to a card (late-injected cards picked up automatically).
- Layout: content column centered on ultra-wide monitors (≥1560px); result values show a dotted underline to signal click-to-convert.
- Also ships the previously-unpushed v5.20.0 unit-consistency sweep (calc-unit-core.js single source of truth, working STRESS STATE card via window.calcStress, Smith principal3) which had been sitting uncommitted since 2026-06-29.
- Tests: `calc/tests/engineer_layer.js` (74 assertions: parser, exact conversions, IMP-map dimensional consistency, solver incl. quantized/negative/impossible cases) + existing `unit_audit.js` (61) — all green. Backup: `backups/amni-calc-deployed/index.html.v5.40.0.bak`. Cache-buster `calc-engineer.js?v=eng1`.

## Amni-Construct v5.28.1 — collinear polygon nodes removed (odd-shape frost footings) - 2026-07-06
- **Anthony's field find (from the Android app!):** extra nodes sitting ON a straight edge (left by the draw tool's ⊕ midpoint handles) read as "corners" to the WASM cores → phantom beam segments + extra frost piers on S-1 for odd-shaped decks.
- **Fix in `shape-edit.js`** (single implementation, copied to deck/patio/pool/floor/roof/frame + _shared; ?v=se3, app.js ?v=hd3): `collinearClean(P, houseEdge)` removes any vertex whose perpendicular deviation from the line through its neighbors is <0.02 ft — EXCEPT the two endpoints of the house edge (the ledger sub-segment on a straight run is semantic, e.g. a 3.5' ledger on a 12' edge). House-edge index remapped through removals; wraparound handled; min 3 vertices. Runs on editor LOAD and on ✓ Use this shape — existing saved shapes self-clean the next time they're applied.
- Verified headless: noisy 12-vertex U → 9 vertices after one apply, ledger node + house_edge preserved, framing-plan element count drops 53→45 and EXACTLY matches a clean-drawn polygon; clean shapes untouched; node unit tests for wraparound + house-edge protection.

## Amni-Calc v5.20.0 — Unit Consistency Sweep (single source of truth) - 2026-06-29
- **Trigger:** "unit issues everywhere — e.g. select lbf and the load on the right shows N." Full audit of all 288 inputs / 26 modules + every output label.
- **Single source of truth `calc/calc-unit-core.js` (`window.UCORE`)** loaded first. Holds the canonical `DIMS` (auto-dropdown factors) + flat `tables` (LEN_TO_MM / FORCE_TO_N / PRESS_TO_MPA / TORQUE_TO_NM / INERTIA_TO_MM4 / …) + `conv/toBase/fromBase/principal3`. `calc-units.js DIMS`, `calc-fixes.js getLen/getForce/getE/getI`, and `calcSpring` multipliers now all derive from it (each keeps an inline fallback). Killed 4 divergent tables.
- **Exact engineering factors** replace rounded ones: lbf = 4.4482216152605 N (was 4.44822), in⁴ = 416231.4256 mm⁴ (was 416231), psi = 0.00689475729316836 MPa, hp = 745.6998715822702 W, etc.
- **Stress module revived + unit-honoring.** `calcStress` never existed in the obfuscated app, so the σx `st-u` selector (MPa/ksi/psi/GPa) and the whole STRESS STATE card did nothing. Implemented `window.calcStress`: reads `st-u` as the unit for all six tensor components, computes principal/von Mises/Tresca/FoS, and **displays results in the selected unit** with matching labels.
- **Principal-stress solver fixed (correctness).** The old cubic (`calc3DPrincipal` + my first calcStress) used an absolute `disc<=1e-9` threshold that collapsed to a hydrostatic triple root at high σ or repeated roots (e.g. 300/300/0 → garbage). Replaced with Smith's magnitude-robust symmetric-3×3 eigenvalue algorithm in `UCORE.principal3`; both stress cards use it.
- **Beam load/support chips** now echo the unit you entered (`100 lbf @ 2 ft`), not the canonical N/kN/mm — the literal "select lbf, see N" symptom. Internal solve stays in N/mm.
- **Verified:** `tests/unit_audit.js` (61 assertions — exact factors, one conversion per category, round-trips, getForce/calcStress/spring/beam-chip paths, principal-stress edge cases) all pass; live browser checks of stress (MPa vs ksi), beam chips, and unchanged bolt/spring/beam compute. Backups in `backups/v5.20.0_calc_units/`.

## [5.24.0] - 2026-06-16 - Amni-Learn module bug sweep: Sudoku unsolvable-puzzle fix + data + anti-repeat
- FULL headless sweep of all 124 module buttons (puppeteer+Edge): init/render pass AND a 14-round click/keypress/canvas interaction storm per module. Result: 124/124 launch + survive interaction with ZERO JS errors. New harnesses learn/tests/layout/{sweep.js,storm.js}.
- BROKEN MODULE FIXED — Sudoku (9x9): generate() removed clues with NO uniqueness check while placeNum()/checkWin() validated against the single hidden solution. On hard/expert this made puzzles with multiple solutions, so a logically-VALID entry got flagged "Wrong!" and auto-erased, and alternate valid completions could never win. Added countSolutions() (respects X-Sudoku diagonals) + uniqueness-gated cell removal (mirrors the correct 4x4 version). Verified: every difficulty in classic AND X mode now uniquely solvable; worst-case gen ~0.9s (expert settles ~25 clues when 22 can't stay unique — valid beats impossible).
- DATA INTEGRITY — audited all 4,875 quiz questions across 16 banks: found + fixed 4 questions with 4 wrong-options (rendered 5 choices) → trimmed to 3 (axolotl, MJO, golden ratio, Pauli exclusion). New harness learn/tests/layout/_qaudit.js (0 issues now).
- ANTI-REPEAT — Scramble/Anagram/Pattern picked random-WITH-replacement (same item could recur immediately). Added a session-persistent no-repeat ring (bounded retry, capped history) so you don't see the same word/puzzle back-to-back. sw cache v1243->v1244.

## [5.19.3] - 2026-06-10 - Calc: shock response spectrum rebuilt on real physics (was saturating at 2.5 G)
- calcShock's SRS clamped the RESPONSE to 2.5 G absolute - Math.min(2.5, |Q|*G) put the amplification-factor cap on factor*G - so any pulse above ~2.5G flatlined (the MIL-STD 50G/11ms default read "2.50 G / 0.05x" at 50 Hz). The closed-form Q also spiked ~5x near ratio 0.5 and decayed to zero at high f_n instead of approaching quasi-static 1.0.
- Replaced with a numeric maximax SRS: RK4 integration of a zeta=0.05 SDOF through the pulse (all four shapes) + analytic residual peak from the end state. 60-point spectrum computes in 9 ms.
- Verified against half-sine SRS theory: 50G/11ms at f_n=50Hz -> 76.31 G / 1.53x (textbook maximax band); quasi-static asymptote 1.04; impulsive region matches 4*fn*tau within 5%; 100G/6ms crash pulse checks out.
- Isolator transmissibility AUDITED CLEAN: r=6, T=0.0333, 96.7% isolation - exact damped formula; resonance card (X_static, X@r=1, Q=1/2zeta) exact.

## [5.19.2] - 2026-06-10 - Calc: weld-group polar J corrected + corner-vector tau_max; five modules hand-verified exact
- calcWeldGroup (overrides layer) used J = (b+d)^3/6 - b^2d^2/(2(b+d)) - the wrong table entry (that subtraction belongs to open/3-sided groups). Full-perimeter rectangle is exactly (b+d)^3/6: defaults now read J_w=1.91e7 mm4 (was 1.63e7), tau_t=23.43 MPa (was 27.50).
- tau_max upgraded from sqrt(tau_d^2+tau_t^2) to the Shigley worst-corner component method (tau_x=Mc_y/J, tau_y=tau_d+Mc_x/J): 27.84 MPa on defaults - matches hand calc digit-for-digit.
- Hand-verified EXACT against textbook formulas: columns (Euler/Johnson sigma_cr=111.03 MPa, P_cr=166.55 kN), shafts (tau=39.8 MPa, N_cr=1337.6 rpm + avoid band), bearings (L10=3375 Mrev = 31,250 h), gears (all five involute diameters + circular pitch), weld deposition (melt->deposit eff + kg/lb conversion + heat input).
- Visual pass: columns/shafts/bearings/gears 3D viewers confirmed live post-resurrection. Queued: vibration isolator transmissibility readout needs a numeric audit.

# Changelog 

## [5.17.0] - 2026-06-10 - Amni-Learn curriculum audit P3/P4: fact + theme fixes, exact dedup (near-dups kept as reinforcement)
- Third/fourth audit pass across the remaining 12 banks. Key judgment call: the agents flagged "hundreds of duplicates" (light-year ×5, vantablack ×5, Mobius ×4 …), but a deterministic byte-exact (question + answer) scan found only **6 truly identical** pairs — the rest are *reworded variants* that function as **intentional spaced reinforcement** across levels, NOT defects, so they were deliberately KEPT (gutting them would hurt retention). Removed the **6 exact duplicates** (weather ×2, counting ×4). **Factual fix**: the music question "Which African drum is hourglass-shaped and squeezed?" was keyed "Djembe / Talking drum" — but a djembe is goblet-shaped and is NOT squeezed; only the **talking drum** fits, so the answer is corrected to "Talking drum" (matches its own explanation). **Theme/neutrality fix**: three **Medusa** myth entries carried both an explicit sexual-assault detail AND modern political editorializing ("victim-blaming in modern reading", "common ancient injustice", "controversial!") — inappropriate for a children's homeschool suite in both respects. Reworded all three to keep the myth accurate and age-appropriate ("punished by Athena after Poseidon offended the goddess in her temple") while dropping the assault detail and the editorial asides. **Deliberately NOT changed**: the Pre-K "Sun is yellow" item (a defensible early-childhood simplification whose own explanation already adds the white-light nuance); near-duplicate reinforcement questions; and the science quantum-at-L4 items (the one agent that flagged them used inconsistent line numbering and a separate thorough review found the science bank factually clean — flagged for a careful manual re-check rather than a risky blind move). **Verified**: node --check clean, classic 8-level smoke + Adventure regression all green. SW cache v1241 → v1242. v5.17.0.

- Anthony asked for a full curriculum review — content level-true per grade band, neutral, TEKS (Texas) / B.E.S.T. (Florida) aligned — for homeschooling his kids. Ran an 8-agent parallel audit across all 16 quiz banks (~4,950 questions). First confirmed all banks ARE structurally grade-banded 1-5 (the 7 "unlevelled-looking" subjects just use 8-space vs 10-space indentation — a false alarm in my extractor). The real damage was concentrated in **MATH** and **COUNTING**, exactly where the "corners-of-a-square → Itô calculus" jump came from. **Applied 206 fixes (140 re-levels + 66 dedup deletes)**: pulled trig, complex numbers, logarithms, calculus, linear algebra, FOIL, and graduate topics (Hilbert spaces, eigenvalues, Riemann zeta) OUT of grades K-5 up to L5 (high-school/STEM) where TEKS/B.E.S.T. place them; pushed basic facts (2+3, place value, skip-counting) that had been padding L4/L5 back DOWN to K-2; deleted 66 true duplicates (triplicated Gödel/Galois/CLT etc.). Retuned Adventure `advPool` backfill threshold (40→12) so battles now stay on-band when a level is healthy (≥12 Qs) instead of over-serving easy review. **Verified**: band-provenance harness now shows grade-3 math battles 100% L3 (zero calculus), grade-5 pure L5, zero calculus at Pre-K; node --check clean; full Adventure regression (56 checks) + classic 8-level smoke ALL green, 0 errors. SW cache v1239 → v1240. v5.15.0. (Remaining audit batches queued: civics/history neutrality + dedup; cross-subject dedup/fact sweep; the 7 eight-space subjects' true-level re-check; and L3/L4 math/counting enrichment.)

## [5.14.1] - 2026-06-09 - Amni-Learn HOTFIX: battle questions now band-pure (no more "corners on a square → Itô calculus")
- Anthony caught a battle escalating from *"how many corners on a square"* to *"what's the product rule"* to *"what is ITÔ CALCULUS"* in one fight. Root causes — **two real bugs**. **(1) Adventure pool design**: `advPool()` concatenated EVERY difficulty tier from the player's band down to level 1 into one bucket, so a Number Peaks battle at STEM band served pre-K counting next to stochastic calculus. Rewritten **band-first**: questions come from the band's own level, backfilling only adjacent *lower* levels when a bank is thin (<40), and the walk-*up* fallback (which could inject college content into low bands) is deleted outright. Each pooled question is provenance-tagged (`_lv`) so the harness can prove origin. **(2) Misleveled curriculum data**: the math bank had a full calculus cluster sitting in **level 3 (grades 3-5!)** — derivative of x², FTC, chain/product rule, Euler's identity — and multivariable calculus (Jacobians, Stokes/Green, Fourier, Gamma function, Taylor series…) in **level 4 (middle school)**. Re-leveled **37 questions**: 35 → L5 (STEM/HS+), 2 (Euler's-number trivia, completing the square) → L4 — this also fixes the CLASSIC band-3/4 math quizzes which were serving the same misleveled content. Anthony's fast-eastern methods (Japanese line multiplication, Trachtenberg) stay at L4 where they belong. Math banks now L1:67/L2:68/L3:60/L4:47/L5:94, zero calculus in L1-L3 (scripted scan). **(3) Label confusion**: the Adventure HUD said "Lv 1 ⟨name⟩" (HERO level) which reads like the AGE band — now "⚔️ Hero Lv N · ⟨name⟩" / "Hero Lv N" in battle. **Verified 6/6** with a new band-provenance harness (`advcheck6.js`): 7-question samples at bands 1/3/5 were 100% level-pure (L1,L1,L1… / L3×7 / L5×7), zero calculus at PRE-K, zero pre-K at STEM (first STEM sample: "What is homological algebra?" — as it should be), HUD disambiguated. Full sweep: M1 16/16, M2 12/12, M3 10/10, M4 10/10, M5 8/8, classic smoke 8/8 — **62 adventure checks green, 0 errors**. SW cache v1238 → v1239. v5.14.1.

## [5.8.135] - 2026-06-09 - Amni-Learn: audit batch B8 — brain-game best scores now persist across sessions

## [5.8.134] - 2026-06-09 - Amni-Learn: audit batch B7 — Circuit Builder now models real circuit topology (no more "any loop lights everything")
- The STEM **Circuit Builder** taught wrong physics. Its test logic ran a single DFS from the battery and, if *any* closed loop existed, lit **every** bulb/LED/motor/buzzer on the canvas — including ones sitting on a dead-end branch that no current could ever reach. A child could wire one real loop and watch unconnected components magically glow, learning a false mental model of how circuits work. **Fixed** by replacing the "is there any loop?" check with a proper **biconnected-component analysis** (`energizedSet()`): a component now lights only if it lies on an actual cycle that includes the battery, computed on a graph with open switches pruned out. So a load on a real loop lights; a load dangling off a dead-end branch stays dark; an open switch correctly kills only the loops that pass through it. The V/I/R readout + buzzer audio now also count only the components actually carrying current. Removed the now-dead `traceCircuit()`. Verified live at L5 by building a battery→LED→resistor loop with a second LED hanging off a dead-end branch, then **pixel-sampling the canvas**: looped LED = [255,255,0] (lit), dead-end LED = [255,107,107] (dark) — exactly correct; readout "✅ Circuit closed! V=12V, I=0.120A, R=100Ω"; **0 errors**, screenshot captured. SW cache v1230 → v1231. v5.8.134.

- Discovered while stress-testing the new per-level curation: the layout harness had only ever run at `level=1` (smallest boards), but several games scale their grid UP with level. **Matching** overflowed the window in **portrait at level 3** (10 pairs / 5 columns) — a real user-reachable bug. Cause: `.m-card` had a fixed `width: clamp(56px,20vw,100px)` (≈82px on a phone) while the grid uses `repeat(cols, 1fr)` tracks; at 5–6 columns the 82px cards far exceeded their ~58px tracks and pushed past the right edge. **Fix:** cards now fill their 1fr track (`width:100%; max-width:100px; min-width:0; aspect-ratio:5/6`) instead of a fixed width, so any column count fits — the `max-width` preserves the larger card look at low levels (3-col PRE-K). Re-ran harness at levels 3 & 5 in both orientations: Matching now `win=-64` portrait / `-298` landscape (fits with margin), **0 overflow**. Verified screenshot: clean 5×4 grid. SW cache v1220 → v1221. v5.8.124.

## [5.8.116] - 2026-06-08 - Amni-Learn: SW network-first for app code (fixes stale-content-after-update)
- **Root cause of "I still see the old version after you shipped a fix."** The service worker's fetch handler was cache-first for EVERYTHING, including `learn-app.js` and `index.html`. So once a device cached the app code, it kept serving that stale copy — bumping the cache name only helped if/when the new SW fully reinstalled and evicted the old cache, which can lag on an installed PWA. Concretely: a device still on the pre-v5.8.103 `learn-app.js` showed the old 40-question L1 Animals bank and TTS'd the 9 no-sound entries that were since removed. **Fix:** the app code (page navigations + `index.html` + `learn-app.js`) is now **network-first** — always fetch the freshest copy when online, update the cache, and fall back to cache only when offline. Static assets (animal mp3s, images, fonts) stay cache-first since they rarely change, so offline/airplane play still works. Verified amni-scient.com already serves the corrected bank (31 questions, all isAudio); this SW change ensures devices actually pick it up. SW cache v1212 → v1213. v5.8.116.

## [5.8.105] - 2026-06-08 - Amni-Learn: fix app-wide back-button cleanup crash
- **The HOME/back button threw on every game exit, silently leaking timers (HIGH).** The `#nav-back` handler referenced `mtnTimer`, a variable that was never declared (a leftover/typo for Auto Miner's actual `window._minerTimer`). So every time you left a game, line `if(mtnTimer){…}` threw `ReferenceError: mtnTimer is not defined`, which **aborted the rest of the cleanup block** — the timers/animations below it (`matchTimer`, `scrTimer`, `_sdkTimer` sudoku, `_spmTimer` speed-math, `_cpTimer` card-pairs, `_stpTimer`, `_nmmTimeout`, `_rxtTimeout`, `_motAnim`, `_pvTimer`) never got cleared and kept running in the background after you returned to the menu. Fixed the reference to `window._minerTimer`, which both stops the crash and restores all the downstream cleanup. Verified: leaving Auto Miner / Speed Math / Sudoku / Scramble / Card Pairs / Cookie Clicker now returns to the menu with 0 console errors (was a ReferenceError each time). Found via a gentle interaction probe (the bulk play-scan only saw it as a protocol timeout on the idle games). SW cache `v1201 → v1202`. `node --check` clean. v5.8.105.

## [5.8.104] - 2026-06-08 - Amni-Learn: play-testing pass — real gameplay bug fixes
- Built an interaction harness (`learn/tests/layout/interact.js`) that drives real gameplay on every module (clicks + arrow/space/enter keys, ~10 steps each) at L1 + L4, capturing JS console/pageerror + post-interaction screenshots, then ran a 4-agent visual review of the played states. Findings fixed:
- **Reaction Lab was completely dead (HIGH).** `initRxnLab`'s animation loop guarded on `currentGame!=='netdebug'` (copy-paste from Net Debug) — since the game is `'rxnlab'` the loop returned immediately and `step()`/`render()` never ran, so the canvas stayed black no matter what you painted. Fixed the guard to `'rxnlab'`; verified particles now paint + react (0→133 rendered pixels in a paint probe). Audited all other `currentGame!==` loop guards — rxnlab was the only mismatch.
- **`ear` (Ear Training) crash.** `_earTone` set `oscillator.frequency.value` to a non-finite value (a NaN midi during rapid mode-switching) → "non-finite AudioParam" pageerror. Added a guard: skip tones with non-finite/≤0 frequency.
- **Math Basics double-answer dupe.** Relied on `pointer-events:none` (which programmatic clicks bypass) to block a second tap — a fast double-tap appended a second explanation + Next block. Added an `answered` flag guard (matches the quiz flow).
- **Speed Math duplicate START button.** Re-init (on mode switch) didn't remove the previous START/PLAY-AGAIN button, stacking duplicates. Gave them a `spm-start` class and clear it on re-init.
- **Quiz "Next" overlapped the explanation text (regression from v5.8.103's sticky-Next).** Reverted Next to a normal block button and capped `.quiz-explain` to `clamp(120px,34vh,300px)` with internal scroll — the explanation stays fully readable and Next sits cleanly below it (card still scrolls so it's always reachable). Re-verified quiz layout 15/15 both orientations, 0 overflow.
- Help/leaderboard overlays flagged by the review were harness artifacts (the bot clicked the help/scores buttons); the "How to Play" modal closes via ✕, "Got it!", or backdrop tap — not a real trap. SW cache `v1200 → v1201`. `node --check` clean. v5.8.104.

## [5.8.103] - 2026-06-08 - Amni-Learn: quiz answer-overflow blocker, L1 animal-sound fix, double-tap-zoom
- **Quiz "can't continue" blocker (P0).** After answering, the explanation panel (`.quiz-explain`, often a long paragraph) + the "Next ▶" button were appended into `#quiz-task-area`, which is `overflow:hidden` and vertically centered — so a long explanation pushed Next *below the card's clipped bottom*, unreachable (reproduced: Next at y=1022 vs card bottom y=870). Fix: `#quiz-task-area{justify-content:flex-start;overflow-y:auto}` so the card scrolls, AND made the "Next ▶" button `position:sticky;bottom:6px` so it's ALWAYS visible at the card bottom regardless of explanation length (verified reachable at initial scroll with a 3468px explanation). 
- **Level-1 Animals: non-animal sounds + TTS (immediate).** The L1 animals bank had grown to 40 entries; 9 of them (Cricket, Dolphin, Goose, Hummingbird, Bat, Penguin, Hyena, Whale, Kookaburra) used sound-words (`Click/Honk/Hum/Bray/Laugh/Song/Chirp-as-cricket`) with **no matching `assets/audio/*.mp3`**, and their words weren't in `playAnimalSound`'s allow-list — so `speakText` fell through to **TTS literally pronouncing the word** (a robot voice saying "Honk"/"Song" = exactly the "non-animal sounds + TTS"). Fix: removed those 9 no-asset entries (honors the pre-K "animal NOISES + IMAGES only" rule), and added the 3 missing mappings (`squeak→mouse, growl→bear, scream→fox`) + allow-list words so Mouse/Bear/Fox play their real MP3s. **L1 animals is now 31 entries, all `isAudio`, every one verified to route to an existing MP3 (0 TTS, 0 text blocks)** via `learn/tests/layout/_animalcheck.js`.
- **Double-tap zoom trap.** Added `touch-action:manipulation` to `html,body,#app,.view,.top-bar` — disables the accidental double-tap-to-zoom (which was getting "stuck" zoomed-in) while KEEPING intentional pinch-zoom for accessibility.
- **Quiz prompt clipped (found via random long-word question).** `#quiz-prompt` was a fixed 2.5rem; long words ("INFRASTRUCTURE") overflowed the card's right edge. Now `clamp(1.25rem,5vw,2.5rem)` + `overflow-wrap/word-break/min-width:0` so any prompt fits (verified with "ANTIDISESTABLISHMENTARIANISM").
- **Landscape visual triage (4 parallel agents over all 124 landscape shots) caught 2 short-height overlaps:** (1) the **clock** ("What time is it?") collapsed to a wide ellipse because the 250px container was `flex-shrink`-ing vertically in the short card, dropping the bottom numbers onto the answer buttons — fixed by a responsive square `SZ=min(250, 42vh, 72vw)` with `flex-shrink:0` and radius/hands/font scaled to `SZ`; (2) **Math Basics** "Show Hint" button was painted over by the `position:sticky` answer-choice row (z-index:20) under `#math-view{justify-content:center}` — fixed in the short-landscape media query (`#math-view` top-aligns, `.math-choices` goes `position:static`). Both re-verified as proper circle / non-overlapping.
- Verified via the screenshot harness (post-answer + clock probed directly) + full re-audit both orientations (124/124, 0 overflow) + parallel visual triage of every shot in both orientations. SW cache `v1199 → v1200`. `node --check` clean. v5.8.103.

## [5.8.102] - 2026-06-08 - Amni-Learn layout-respect overhaul (every module fits its card)
- **Trigger (Anthony):** modules didn't respect sizing/borders — boards fell out of the window or resized per round; top bar crowded; "use screen grabs yourself to confirm." Built a screenshot harness (`learn/tests/layout/harness.js`, puppeteer-core + Edge) that serves the site, drives **every** `.game-btn` (incl. all life subgames + quiz subjects, ~124 modules) at landscape (880×412) and portrait (412×880) phone viewports, measures window- AND card-overflow (excluding intentional `overflow-x:auto` swipe lanes), and screenshots each. Baseline → 124 modules audited per orientation + parallel visual triage of all 248 shots.
- **Root cause:** board/grid/arena games computed cell/arena size from a hardcoded constant (`Math.min(MAX,Math.floor(380/n))`, `width:min(96vw,…)`) instead of the card width, so on phones they overflowed/clipped `#life-task-area`. The existing global clamp only limited to the **viewport**, never the **card**.
- **Fixes (`learn-app.js`):** added `_boardCell(n,maxCell,gap,pad)` (container-relative cell sizer) and replaced all 5 fixed-constant board calcs (sliding, 2048, sudoku, minesweeper, memory-match, lights-out family); fixed `96vw`/`88vw` arenas (bubble-pop, same-or-different) to card-relative. Added `_fitToCard()` — a universal backstop that scales any board/grid/arena exceeding its card and **re-fits on every DOM rebuild / resize / orientationchange** (MutationObserver on `#app` + resize hooks), which also kills the "resizes per round" inconsistency for the whole suite. Demoted non-celebration toasts (theme toggle, spaced-rep hint) from the full-screen `#feedback` celebration to a small bottom-pill `_toast()` (fixes the "Amber theme" overlay slapped over gameplay); game-win celebrations unchanged. Vacuum: HUD pinned above sprites + dirt spawns below it.
- **Fixes (`index.html` CSS):** `#mini-toast` bottom pill; robust narrow-width top bar (≤560/≤380: tighten gaps, truncate/hide profile chip, no overlap); short-landscape (`max-height:520px`) title/padding shrink so more fits above the fold; card max-width clamps; `.retro-hud` now wraps+centers (was an un-wrapping flex row pushing the 🏆 Scores button off-screen in Block Drop/Invaders); `#music-view .piano-wrap` capped to its parent (id-scoped to beat the universal clamp's specificity) so the keyboard scrolls instead of poking off-screen.
- **Verified:** re-ran the harness both orientations — **landscape 124/124 and portrait 124/124 with 0 window-overflow and 0 card-overflow**; screenshots retained as per-module proof (`learn/tests/layout/shots*/`). Plan/council: `docs/checklists/checklist_layout_respect_v5.8.102.md` + `docs/guardian_councils/guardian_council_layout_respect.md`. Backups `backups/{index.html,learn-app.js,sw.js}.v5.8.102.bak`. SW cache `amni-learn-v1198 → v1199`. `node --check` clean. v5.8.102.

## [5.8.87] - 2026-06-02 - Bugfix: gate auto-restart so exiting mid-restart can't leak/clobber
- Subtle edge case: Vacuum, Matching, and Dishes auto-restart via `setTimeout(initX, ~2.2s)` after a win. `goBack`'s cleanup clears timers but can't cancel a pending setTimeout — so exiting during that window let the restart fire *after exit*, re-initializing the game into a hidden (or different) view. For the timer-bearing games (Vacuum's `_vacTimer`, Matching's `matchTimer`) that re-init also created a fresh `setInterval` that `goBack` had already passed → an orphaned timer leak; worse, if you'd switched to another life sub-game, the restart could clobber it. Gated each auto-restart on the game still being active (`currentGame`/`currentSubgame`), so it no-ops if you've left. Bumps sw v1185→v1186. v5.8.87.

## [5.8.86] - 2026-06-02 - Bugfix: Reaction Lab leaked a document mouseup listener per open
- A `document.addEventListener` audit found the sibling of the Word Search leak: the **Reaction Lab** (`initRxnLab`) added an **anonymous** `document.addEventListener('mouseup', …)` on every open — anonymous, so unremovable, accumulating a global mouseup handler (and retaining the old closure) each time. Fixed with a stored, deduplicated handler (`window._rxnMouseUp` + remove-then-add). Other `document` listeners verified clean: fullscreenchange (one-time top-level), 2048 keydown (already remove-then-add). Bumps sw v1184→v1185. v5.8.86.

## [5.8.85] - 2026-06-02 - Bugfix: Word Search leaked a window pointerup listener per open
- A `window.addEventListener` audit found one accumulation leak: **Word Search** added `window.addEventListener('pointerup', _wsEnd)` on every open (with a fresh `_wsEnd` closure each time) and never removed it — so each re-open stacked another global listener and retained the old grid/closure in memory (same bug class as the keydown-accumulation fix). The grid-element listeners are fine (they die with the replaced grid); the window listener is needed to end a selection when you release the pointer off the grid, so fixed with remove-then-add idempotency (`window._wsEndHandler`). Now only ever one. Other window listeners verified: top-level one-time (pointermove/keydown/load/confetti-resize) or already remove-then-add (TD/2048/cblast canvas resizes). Bumps sw v1183→v1184. v5.8.85.

## [5.8.84] - 2026-06-02 - Robustness: guard unguarded JSON.parse(localStorage) sites
- Audited all 15 `JSON.parse(localStorage/sessionStorage…)` sites for crash-on-corrupt-data. Most were already guarded (achievement state, high-scores, the t2048/cblast/TD save-loaders, quiz missed-map, `_solvedSet`), but **four parsed unguarded** — corrupt or partially-written storage would throw and break the game on load. Fixed: **Cookie Clicker** (`ck-ach`/`ck-up`) and **Garden Grower** (`gd-ach`/`gd-up`) now use a safe-parse helper **plus `Array.isArray` checks** (so a valid-but-non-array value can't throw on `.forEach`); **Minesweeper** (`ms-best`) and the **chemistry reaction tracker** (`rxn-discovered`) wrapped in try/catch IIFEs. Defensive only — normal play unaffected. Bumps sw v1182→v1183. v5.8.84.

## [5.8.83] - 2026-06-02 - Bugfix: Net Debug rAF loop leaked after exit
- A `requestAnimationFrame`-loop audit (27 rAF sites vs 16 cancels) found one real leak: the **Net Debug** game's loop (`function loop(){step();step();render();animId=requestAnimationFrame(loop);}`) re-scheduled itself **unconditionally** and its `animId` was never cancelled (a local var, so `goBack`'s cleanup couldn't reach it). Exiting the game left the loop running forever, and re-entering **stacked** loops — a compounding CPU/GPU drain. Fixed with a `if(currentGame!=='netdebug')return;` gate (same pattern as Pull-the-Pin / Fill-the-Cup), so the loop self-terminates on exit. Audited all other rAF sites: gated (pullpin/fillcup/bubble-pop), cancelled (breakout/pong/invaders/flappy/TD/dots/MOT/colorblast), or one-shot (confetti/font-fit) — all fine. Bumps sw v1181→v1182. v5.8.83.

## [5.8.61] - 2026-06-01 - NEW GAME: 🟤 Mancala (Kalah) vs AI
- Sixth new arcade game — the standout *missing* classic, and a great fit for a learning app (real counting + strategy, non-grid sowing mechanic distinct from the board games already added). Standard Kalah: 6 pits + a store per side, 4 seeds each. Tap one of your pits to scoop + sow seeds counterclockwise (into your own store, skipping the opponent's). Land your last seed in your store → **extra turn**; land in your own empty pit → **capture** that seed plus the seeds directly across. Game ends when a side empties; remaining seeds sweep to their owner; most seeds wins.
- **AI:** evaluates all 6 of its moves one-ply (store gain ×2 + extra-turn bonus + capture bonus) via snapshot/apply/restore, and chains its own extra turns. All loops bounded: the sow loop advances every step and decrements on each non-skipped drop (≤~52 iters), AI eval is 6 pits, and the AI extra-turn chain is capped (`aiChain<20`) and `currentGame`-gated — no freeze risk. Win tally persists (`mc-wins`, distinct from Map Clicker's `mc-best-round-*`) + new **🟤 Mancala Master** achievement. Carries a NEW badge. ## [5.8.51] - 2026-06-01 - HOTFIX: Count It! infinite-loop freeze when count was 1
- Self-review of the just-shipped Count It! (5.8.50) caught a CRITICAL bug before it could bite users: the distractor generator `while(opts.size<4){const d=count+rand(−2..2);...}` could never reach 4 distinct options when `count===1` (the ±2 window yields only {1,2,3}), causing an **infinite loop that freezes the browser** — and count=1 occurs ~1-in-5 rounds at Level 1. 
- Fixed with a guarded random loop (`guard++<60`, widened to ±3) PLUS a guaranteed fallback fill (`let f=1; while(opts.size<4){if(f!==count)opts.add(f);f++;}`) that always completes the option set deterministically. No infinite loop is now possible for any count. (Lesson: even a structure-mirroring new game needs its NEW logic — here, distractor math near boundaries — reviewed.) node --check passes. Bumps sw v1150→v1151. v5.8.51.

## [5.8.44] - 2026-06-01 - BUG: 6 arcade games doubled keyboard input after re-opening (listener leak)
- The bug class exposed by the Fill the Cup fix (5.8.43) turned out to affect **6 existing, reachable arcade games**: Snake, Breakout, Pong, Space Invaders, Block Drop (Tetris), and Flappy Jump each registered controls via `document.addEventListener('keydown', <anonymous>)` on every init and never removed the handler. So each time you re-opened (or left and returned to) one of these games in a session, another copy of its key handler stacked up — and since most actions are RELATIVE (`px--`, `py-=18`, `tap()`, `bullets.push`, `rotate()`), the inputs MULTIPLIED: Tetris pieces jumping 2+ cells per arrow press, Flappy double-flapping, Invaders multi-firing, paddles lurching. (All correctly guard `currentGame`, so they never cross-fired between games — the bug was strictly per-game re-open multiplication.)
- Fixed all six by switching to `document.onkeydown = <handler>` (single-slot; each init cleanly replaces the prior), matching Sudoku/Fill the Cup. The 2048 game was already correct (named handler + removeEventListener + guard) and is untouched; it's the only remaining `addEventListener('keydown')` and coexists fine (separate listener slot, both guard currentGame). node --check passes. Bumps sw v1143→v1144. v5.8.44.

## [5.8.43] - 2026-06-01 - Harden Fill the Cup: keydown listener no longer accumulates on re-open
- Responsible follow-through on surfacing Fill the Cup (5.8.42): it registered its spacebar control via `document.addEventListener('keydown', …)`, which ADDS a new handler every time the game initializes and never removes it. While the game was dead code this never mattered, but now that it's reachable, re-opening it would stack handlers — each guards on `currentGame==='fillcup'`, so when the game is active ALL accumulated copies fire and a single spacebar press would pour/toggle multiple times. Changed to `document.onkeydown = …` (single-slot replace, the same pattern the 9×9 Sudoku uses), so each init cleanly supersedes the prior handler — no accumulation. (Pull the Pin was already safe: its listener is on the canvas, which is destroyed + recreated each init.)
- Verified scans this round are otherwise clean: no orphaned init functions remain (pullpin/fillcup were the last), and every `data-game` has both a dispatcher case AND a `views` registry entry. node --check passes. Bumps sw v1142→v1143. v5.8.43.

## [5.8.36] - 2026-06-01 - A11Y: modal focus management (completes the dialog pattern)
- Final piece of the WAI-ARIA dialog pattern (after Escape-to-close 5.8.34 + dialog semantics 5.8.35): **focus now moves into a modal when it opens and returns to the trigger when it closes**. Previously, opening Profile/Stats/etc. left keyboard focus stranded on the button *behind* the overlay, and closing didn't restore it.
- Implemented centrally with a single `MutationObserver` on `document.body` (no edits to the 6 modal creation sites): on a `.hs-overlay` being added it stores `document.activeElement` and focuses the `.hs-modal` container (`tabindex=-1`, `preventScroll`) — the container, NOT the first input, so the mobile keyboard doesn't pop open; on removal it restores focus to the stored trigger. Fast classList short-circuit keeps it cheap despite cursor-trail particles also being body children. node --check passes. Bumps sw v1135→v1136. v5.8.36.

## [5.8.30] - 2026-06-01 - PWA FIX: link the manifest so Amni-Learn is actually installable
- Real functional bug: `learn/manifest.webmanifest` existed (and was even precached by the service worker), but **`learn/index.html` never linked it** — no `<link rel="manifest">` in the head. So browsers never read the PWA metadata, and "Add to Home Screen" produced a generic bookmark instead of a standalone app with the proper name, icons, theme color, and display mode. The service worker itself was registering fine (learn-app.js:2793), so offline caching worked — but installability was silently broken.
- Added `<link rel="manifest" href="manifest.webmanifest">` plus the supporting meta tags: `theme-color` (#4db8ff, matching the manifest), `apple-mobile-web-app-capable` / `mobile-web-app-capable` (standalone launch on iOS/Android), `apple-mobile-web-app-status-bar-style`, and `apple-mobile-web-app-title`. Amni-Learn now installs as a real PWA (offline-capable kids' learning app on the home screen). node --check passes (HTML head edit in learn/index.html). Bumps sw v1129→v1130. v5.8.30.

## [5.8.27] - 2026-06-01 - A11Y: feedback toast announced to screen readers (aria-live)
- The on-screen feedback toast (`#feedback` — shows "Correct!", "Try again!", combo/score messages on every answer) was a plain `<div>` with no live-region semantics, so screen-reader users got NO spoken confirmation of right/wrong at any level. Added `role="status" aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true"` so each feedback message is announced when it changes — the standard ARIA mechanism, complementing (not replacing) the Level-1 speech-synthesis TTS that serves sighted pre-readers.
- "polite" (not "assertive") queues announcements without interrupting, appropriate for status feedback; "atomic" reads the whole message. node --check passes (HTML attribute-only change in learn/index.html). Bumps sw v1126→v1127. v5.8.27.

## [5.8.19] - 2026-06-01 - TTS ROBUSTNESS: warm + cache the voice (fixes iPad cold-start)
- On iOS Safari (the likely device for a toddler) `speechSynthesis.getVoices()` returns `[]` until the async `voiceschanged` event fires — so the very first quiz question of a fresh session could speak in the wrong/default voice or be dropped. Now we **warm voices on load** (`getVoices()` call kicks the async fetch) and cache the chosen voice once `voiceschanged` fires, so by the time a kid reaches a game the friendly voice is ready.
- Also a small perf win: `_ttsVoice()` was re-scanning the entire system voice list on *every* utterance; it now returns a cached pick (`_ttsVoiceCache`, refreshed on `voiceschanged`). Split out `_ttsPickVoice(vs)` for the preference logic. Pure additive, graceful if speechSynthesis is absent. node --check passes. Bumps sw v1118→v1119. v5.8.19.

## [5.8.18] - 2026-06-01 - TTS QUALITY: warm child-friendly voice for all pre-K speech
- All the pre-K read-aloud (`speakSeq`/`speakText` — quiz, math, games, tutorials, feedback) used `_ttsVoice()`, which just grabbed any `en-US localService` voice — on Windows that's often the robotic default ("Microsoft David"). Meanwhile the **Storybook** already hand-picked a warm, friendly voice (Samantha / Aria / Jenny / Google US English…). Upgraded `_ttsVoice()` to prefer that SAME friendly list first (added Microsoft Zira — the common Windows female voice — plus Moira/Tessa/Fiona for macOS/other), then any en-US female, then en-US local, then any en, then null. So every game and quiz now speaks in the same gentle voice as the Storybook instead of a stiff default — a consistency + warmth win across the whole TTS layer built in 5.8.1–5.8.17.
- Pure fallback chain (graceful if no named voice exists). node --check passes. Bumps sw v1117→v1118. v5.8.18.

## [5.7.9997] - 2026-06-01 - AUDIT FIX: stale miss-timeout in Go/No-Go + Spotlight (Posner)
- Consolidation/self-audit pass over the 11 new modules + theme system. Found a real concurrency bug in the two modules that auto-advance on no-response (Go/No-Go, Spotlight/Posner): when the stimulus appeared they scheduled a "miss" timeout in window._gngTimeout/_posTimeout, but on a user RESPONSE that handle was overwritten by the next-trial timeout WITHOUT clearing the pending miss. On a fast response with a long response window (esp. low levels), the stale miss-timeout could fire during the NEXT trial (awaiting=true again) → false miss + an extra next() → corrupted trial count/sequence.
- Fix: in both respond() handlers, clearTimeout the pending miss-timeout immediately after setting awaiting=false, before scheduling the next trial. Now a response cleanly cancels its own trial's miss-timeout. (Flanker/Simon/TaskSwitch/ChangeDet/Numerosity are purely response-driven with no auto-advance timeout, so they were already safe; verified.)
- Theme system audited: toggle + Profile picker both route through _applyTheme which handles all ids; clean themes work alongside the Amni unlock themes. (Minor enhancement noted, not a bug: clean themes don't yet appear in the Profile theme picker list — toggle-only for now.)
- node --check passes. Bumps sw v1086→v1087. v5.7.9997.

## [5.7.998] - 2026-06-01 - NEW MODULE: Tower of London (planning / executive function) — last of the 3
- Brain-exercise #9, completing Anthony's "add the last 3" list. Tower of London — the classic PLANNING test (executive function); distinct from the existing Tower of Hanoi (Hanoi is size-ordered recursion; ToL is arbitrary colored-ball goals).
- Gameplay: 3 pegs, 3 colored balls; a Goal mini-display shows the target. Tap a peg to lift its top ball, tap another to drop (cap 3/peg). Match the goal in as few moves as possible. The engine runs a BFS over the full state graph to compute the OPTIMAL move count, shown live as "Best path"; matching it = PERFECT. Score rewards efficiency. "NEW PUZZLE" reshuffles.
- Level-scaled: goal is chosen from the BFS distance bucket — L1-2 ≈ 2 optimal moves, L3 ≈ 4, L4-5 ≈ 5. Lvl HUD chip + bounce-in board. Turn-based (no timers), so cleanup is just the `currentGame!=='tol'` guard in pegClick.

## [5.7.962] - 2026-06-01 - HARDEN bubble-pop fix: reset flag in shared cleanupLifeGame (all exit paths)
- Follow-up to v5.7.961: moved `window._bubActive=false` out of the nav-back handler and into the shared `cleanupLifeGame()`, which runs on BOTH exit paths — the back button AND a direct game-switch (called right before any new sub-game inits). This guarantees the bubble loop stops no matter how the user leaves it, not just via Back. (initBubblePop re-sets the flag true after cleanup, so launching/restarting Bubble Pop still works.)
- Verified the other animation games don't have this leak: TD/fillcup/pullpin loops self-guard with `currentGame!==` checks; breakout/pong/invaders/flappy/motion store cancellable AF handles cleared in teardown; none call the GLOBAL showFeedback from an uncancelled loop the way bubble-pop did.

## [5.7.961] - 2026-06-01 - BUGFIX (Anthony report): Bubble Pop leak + empty end screen
- BUG 1 (functional, serious): exiting Bubble Pop mid-round kept flashing "Missed it!" over the NEXT module. Cause: each bubble runs its own requestAnimationFrame loop; the central nav-back teardown clears every game's setInterval / cancelAnimationFrame handles, but bubble-pop's per-bubble rAF loops had no handle, so they kept running — a target bubble floating off called onMiss → showFeedback('Missed it!') → nextRound() → spawned more bubbles into the (now-detached) arena, forever. FIX: added a window._bubActive cancellation flag — set true in initBubblePop, set FALSE in the nav-back teardown, and checked in tick() (stop animating), nextRound() (don't spawn), and onMiss() (don't flash). Exiting now fully stops the game.
- BUG 2 (visual): the end screen ("NEW BEST! / X/10 popped correctly") sat top-aligned in the fixed-height arena, leaving a big empty blue box. FIX: vertically center the end content (arena flex-center), reverted to normal block layout when gameplay rounds resume.
- node --check passes. Bumps sw v1041→v1042. v5.7.961.

## [5.7.321] - 2026-05-26 - Aggressive mobile overflow patch (round 2)
- Fixed dvh/vh order bug on line 1220: `body.game-active #app{height:100dvh;height:100vh}` had dvh declared FIRST → modern Safari resolved to vh (URL-bar-collapsed height = taller than visible), causing every game module to overflow below viewport. Inverted to `100vh;100dvh` so dvh wins.
- Added `min-height:100dvh` to #app baseline (matches body).
- Aggressive @media ≤768px clamp: EVERY descendant of .view enforces `max-width:100vw !important` (catches all the deeply-nested inline-styled containers we can\'t enumerate). Excludes [data-hscroll] + canvas.
- iOS safe-area-insets: top-bar pads under notch, body bottom-pad under home indicator.
- Tables/pre/code in .view force display:block + overflow-x:auto to prevent long content from busting parent.

## [5.7.98] - 2026-05-25 - Sudoku 4×4: guarantee unique solution
- **Anthony reported**: "second sudoku game I've played with two sets of pairs at the end, where either answer would technically work."
- **Root cause**: my v5.7.83 Sudoku generator removed cells naively. With 4 cells given (Hard), the remaining puzzle can have multiple valid completions — meaning at the end the player faces a literal coin-flip between equally-valid answers. Bad puzzle design.
- **Fix**: added a `countSolutions(grid, cap)` backtracking solver (caps at 2 for efficiency — once we see 2 solutions, we know the puzzle isn't unique). Generator now removes cells ONE AT A TIME, and only commits the removal if the puzzle remains uniquely solvable. Otherwise the cell is restored. Loop continues until the difficulty target is hit OR no more cells can be removed without losing uniqueness.
- **Effect**: every Sudoku 4×4 puzzle now has exactly one solution. Hard may occasionally show 5–6 givens instead of 4 (when 4 givens would be ambiguous) — that's intentional and correct.
- **SW cache v176 → v177**.

## [5.7.97] - 2026-05-25 - Chess P4 + P6 pre-move legality fix
- **Anthony reported**: "chess puzzle 6 starts with enemy king in check which is silly".
- A programmatic sweep of all 42 puzzles found **2 bugs**, both same flaw — white queen already attacking the black king BEFORE the puzzle move, which means Black just played a move that left their king in check (illegal). Awkward.
- **P4** (was `{g6:'K',h5:'Q',h8:'k'}, sol:'h5-h7'`): Qh5 attacks Kh8 along the h-file pre-move. → Fixed: move queen to **f7** (no line of attack on h8 pre-move), sol becomes `f7-h7` (queen slides along the 7th rank, lands on h7 defended by Kg6).
- **P6** (was `{c6:'K',a6:'Q',c8:'k'}, sol:'a6-a8'`): Qa6 attacks Kc8 along the a6-c8 diagonal pre-move (a6-b7-c8 path clear). → Fixed: move queen to **a1**, sol becomes `a1-a8` (queen rolls UP the empty a-file, lands on a8 with the same 8th-rank+king mating geometry).
- Re-ran the sweep: **all 42 puzzles now have legal pre-move positions**. Verifier script is `node -e "..."` over `_chessPuzzles`; saving snippet to incorporate into a pre-flight check.
- **SW cache v175 → v176**.

## [5.7.60] - 2026-05-21 - Tower of Hanoi (Life Skills)
- New Life Skills subgame: **🗼 Tower of Hanoi** — the classic recursive math/logic puzzle.
- **Mechanics**:
  - 3 pegs on a sky-blue board. Start: all disks stacked on the left peg in size order (largest at bottom).
  - Tap a peg → picks up its top disk (peg highlights gold). Tap another peg → drops the disk there.
  - **Rule**: bigger disk can never sit on a smaller one. Violation shows feedback and unselects.
  - Win when all disks are on the right peg.
- **Disk count picker**: **3 / 4 / 5 / 6 / 7 disks** (optimal solutions: 7, 15, 31, 63, 127 moves respectively — 2ⁿ−1).
- HUD shows move count + optimal target + best-ever for the current disk count (`hanoi-best-N` per size).

## [5.7.59] - 2026-05-21 - Code Lock — Mastermind-style deduction (Life Skills)
- New Life Skills subgame: **🔐 Code Lock** — classic adult brain-exercise deduction game.
- **Mechanics**:
  - Computer picks a hidden **4-color code** from 6 options (🔴🟠🟡🟢🔵🟣), repeats allowed.
  - User has **10 guesses**. Each: pick 4 colors from the palette (auto-fills the empty slot left-to-right), then Submit.
  - Feedback per guess:
    - **⚫ Black peg** = one color is in the right spot.
    - **⚪ White peg** = one color is in the code but in the wrong spot.
    - No peg = color not in code.
  - Each row of the history shows the guess + feedback so the player can deduce the code.
- Win condition: 4 black pegs (perfect guess). `cl-best` stores fewest guesses-to-crack across all games; NEW BEST banner if you beat it.
- Loss: 10 guesses without success — reveals the code.
- Pure logic deduction, ~5–10 minute games. Distinct from every other Life subgame.

## [5.7.52] - 2026-05-21 - AI Ethics Debug: +2 ML scenarios (11 → 13)
- Two new production-ML failure-mode scenarios, framed as engineering issues:
  - **Catastrophic Forgetting** — vision model trained sequentially on dogs → cats → birds; after the last round it can't classify dogs/cats anymore. The "Recent Bias" input dominates; old-task features starved. Solution: cut Recent Bias ≤0.2, boost Dog/Cat Features ≥0.4. Impact references McCloskey & Cohen 1989, elastic weight consolidation (Kirkpatrick 2017), experience replay buffers.
  - **Data Poisoning** — spam classifier where attackers injected mislabeled samples. The "Poisoned Cluster" input drags the model away from real spam signals. Solution: cut Poisoned Cluster ≤0.2, boost URL Reputation ≥0.5 and Sender History ≥0.4. Impact references Biggio et al. 2012, RANSAC-style outlier filtering, data provenance.

## [5.7.49] - 2026-05-21 - Chess: pawn promotion mate (29 → 30)
- **P30 Pawn promotion mate** — `a7-a8#` (promotes to queen) with Ka1 / Pa7 / Nh5 / Bf5 vs Kh8.
- Tactical motif: an underdog white pawn pushes to a8, promotes to a queen, and the new queen attacks h8 along the 8th rank.
- Escape verification:
  - **g7**: Nh5 attacks (h5→g7 is a valid knight move).
  - **h7**: Light-squared bishop on f5 covers along the f5-g6-h7 diagonal (all light, all empty).
  - **g8**: Qa8 covers along the 8th rank.
  - **Capture queen**: Kh8 to a8 is 7 squares — impossible.
  - **Block**: No black pieces left.
- The chess engine handles promotion implicitly — it matches the `a7-a8` move string regardless of resulting piece, so the puzzle works without engine changes.
- Brings the chess bank to a round **30 puzzles**.

## [5.7.31] - 2026-05-20 - Chess: +2 puzzles, new tactical patterns (22 → 24)

## [5.7.20] - 2026-05-20 - AI Ethics Debug: +3 ML-engineering scenarios (8 → 11)
- Adding three production-ML failure-mode scenarios to NetDebug, all framed as engineering issues (no DEI language per project convention):
  - **Class Imbalance** — 0.1% positive class anomaly detector with a "Default Bias" pull toward the majority class. Solution: cut the bias input, boost Pattern Match (≥0.5) and Statistical Outlier (≥0.4). Impact note covers focal loss, SMOTE, and PR-curve threshold tuning.
  - **Reward Hacking** — RL agent rewarded on Frame Score exploits a counter-overflow glitch instead of actually playing. Solution: cut the Frame Score signal, reward Goal Distance and Survival Time. Impact references Amodei et al. 2016 "Concrete Problems in AI Safety."
  - **Calibration Failure** — 95% accuracy but "90% confident" means 70% in practice; a "Confidence Boost" input pumps outputs without evidence. Solution: cut Confidence Boost, boost Feature Match and Evidence Score. Impact covers temperature scaling, Platt scaling, isotonic regression.

## [5.7.14] - 2026-05-20 - AI Ethics Debug: 5 → 8 scenarios
- AI Ethics Debug now has 8 ML failure-mode scenarios (was 5). Added in neutral ML-engineering framing per project policy:
  - 📉 **Survivor Bias** — stock-return predictor trained only on still-listed firms over-weights "Years Listed" while bankrupted companies are missing from the training set. Cut the leaky filter feature and lean on Revenue Growth + Operating Margin.

- Each new scenario follows the established format: title, technical description, input/hidden/output network, initial connection weights, `check()` validator, hint progression, real-world impact citation (Sugiyama 2007 for shift, mutual-fund survivor-bias study, recommender feedback-loop literature).

## [5.7.6] - 2026-05-19 - Chess puzzles 8 & 10 unsound
- **Puzzle 8** (added v5.6.78): `{c7:'K',b6:'P',b1:'Q',a8:'k'}` → `Qb1-b8`. The white pawn on b6 blocks the queen's b-file path from b1 to b8. Queen can't pass through own pawn. Invalid solution.
  - **Fix**: replace defender with a bishop on c5 — same role (covers a7 along the c5-a7 diagonal, b6 now empty) but doesn't block the queen path. Position is now `{c7:'K',c5:'B',b1:'Q',a8:'k'}`, sol unchanged `b1-b8`.
- **Puzzle 10** (added v5.6.78): `{g1:'K',e5:'N',h8:'k',g8:'n',g7:'r',h7:'p'}` → `Ne5-f7`. The black rook on g7 attacks f7 along the 7th rank, so it can capture the mating knight. Not a smothered mate.
  - **Fix**: replace the rook on g7 with a black pawn. Pawn on g7 only attacks f6/h6 (forward-diagonally downward for black) and doesn't reach f7. Knight on g8 also doesn't reach f7 (g8 knight attacks e7/f6/h6). King too far. True smothered mate — all escapes blocked by own pieces, no capturer. Position: `{g1:'K',e5:'N',h8:'k',g8:'n',g7:'p',h7:'p'}`.
- Re-verified all 8 puzzles I added in v5.6.78 once more (king escape squares all attacked or occupied, mating piece defended where capturable, no line-of-sight pieces blocking the move). 6 were already clean; these 2 are now fixed.

## [5.7.3] - 2026-05-19 - Money Math: real L1-L5 progression
- **Bug**: L4 and L5 were near-clones of L3 — same prices ($1.99-$9.99), same denominations, only the prompt string differed ("Paid $X — Give back:"). Anthony reported L5 felt like "L2 stuff" because the actual math complexity didn't progress past L3.
- **Fix**: each level now has distinct mechanics and pricing tiers:
  - **L1 Count the Coins** — single item priced 5¢-99¢, coins only (penny/nickel/dime/quarter). Same as before, expanded pool 8 → 12 items.
  - **L2 Count the Money** — single item $1.75-$12.50, full denomination set (coins + $1/$5/$10/$20).
  - **L3 Make Change** — item priced $1.99-$9.99, paid with rounded-up dollar, give exact change. Denomination set is intentionally restricted (no $10/$20) so the user has to actually build small change.
  - **L4 Cart Total + Sales Tax** (NEW). Cart of 2-3 random items, subtotal printed, 8% sales tax added, total shown. User must pay the exact post-tax total. Combines mental addition + percentage application.
  - **L5 Doing Your Taxes** (NEW — per Anthony's "by L5 you should be doing taxes" directive). Paystub scenario: random gross paycheck ($800-$3500), Federal income tax rate ($10/12/15/18/22%), State tax (0/3/4/5/6%), FICA fixed 7.65%. User computes total withholding and pays that amount. L5 tray includes $50 + $100 bills since totals can reach $1000+.
- Per-level scoring scales with cognitive load: L1=1, L2=1, L3=3, L4=5, L5=6 (was uniform 1 or 3).

## [5.6.91] - 2026-05-19 - Visual Search: 🧬 Conjunction task (Treisman)
- Visual Search had only one task: find a single-feature target among uniform distractors (e.g., a Q among Os — pop-out, near-constant RT regardless of grid size). Now adds a second task tier from cognitive psychology:
  - 🔍 **Feature** (default, original) — single distinguishing feature; pop-out search.
  - 🧬 **Conjunction** — target defined by a combination (color + letter). Distractors share *one* feature each: half match the target color but have the wrong letter, half match the target letter but have the wrong color. Neither attribute alone identifies the target — classic Treisman feature-integration task. RT scales linearly with set size (vs constant for pop-out).
- 5 conjunction sets across distinct color/letter pairs: red-X / blue-O, green-T / yellow-L, purple-Z / teal-N, orange-★ / blue-○, red-◆ / green-□.
- Score weight bumped for conjunction (faster = more points; 4/3/2 vs feature's 3/2/1).
- Best avg-RT tracked per (task, mode): `vs-best-avg-conjunction-hard`, etc. Falls back to original `vs-best-avg-<mode>` keys for first run.
- Intro text and target-card chip adapt to the active task.
- **SW cache v72 → v73** to flush.

## [5.6.78] - 2026-05-19 - Chess Puzzles: 7 → 15 puzzles (more patterns)
- Doubled the mate-in-1 bank from 7 to 15 puzzles. Eight new positions span:
  - **Queen + king + pawn cage** (Pb6 covering a7 while the queen takes b8 against Ka8).
  - **Rook box** with king-on-f6 — the white king covers e7/f7/g7 so a rook arrives unopposed on the 8th rank.
  - **Smothered mate** — the textbook position where black's own knight (g8), rook (g7), and pawn (h7) jail the king at h8 and Nf7 delivers.
  - **Rook + pawn shield** — Pg7 defends Rh8 from a king capture; Ra7 cuts the 7th rank.
  - **Queen + knight battery** — Nh5 defends Qg7 so the king cannot take.
  - **Back-rank mate variant** — three black pawns at f7/g7/h7 trap the king and the rook delivers down the a-file.
  - **Long-diagonal queen mate** — Q swings from h5 to e8 with king-and-pawn support cutting a7.
  - **Q + K vs K** edge mate — clean Qa8 finish with the king cutting every escape.
- Each puzzle individually verified: defender present on the mating square (if the king could capture), every king escape square is attacked or occupied, no illegal initial position (no implicit pre-check).
- **SW cache v59 → v60** to flush.

## [5.6.77] - 2026-05-19 - NEW MODULE: Ear Training (intervals, chords, note ID)
- Final module from the May 2026 expansion plan. Brain-cognitive category, 🎼 icon.
- **3 modes**:
  - 🎵 **Intervals** — hear two notes ascending; identify the interval (unison through octave). Replay button + "hear harmonic" button so the user can compare ascending and stacked.

## [5.6.76] - 2026-05-19 - Light-mode pass + Morse Code Trainer
- **Bug — light mode was broken inside modules**: theme toggle only flipped chrome/menu surfaces; every game/quiz view kept its hardcoded dark backgrounds (#1b1e23, #1e252b, #221f26, …) and every JS-injected panel used inline `color:#ecf0f1` / dark rgba fills, so module screens stayed charcoal even after toggling to ☀️.
- **Fix — comprehensive light-mode pass**:
  - Introduced CSS theme variables: `--text`, `--text-muted`, `--panel-bg`, `--panel-border`, `--bg-deep`, `--bg-panel-deep`, `--accent`. Dark mode keeps the original neon defaults; `body.light-mode` overrides them so anything using `var(...)` flips automatically.
  - Swept the file replacing the 50 hardcoded `color:#ecf0f1` (and `color: #ecf0f1`) inline-style instances with `color:var(--text,#ecf0f1)` so JS-built modules pick up the active theme without a per-init refactor.
  - Added per-view light-mode background overrides for all 30+ module views (#sudoku-view, #stroop-view, #chess-view, #morse-view, etc.). Each flips to `#f5f7fa` on light. The intentionally CRT-styled retro arcade titles still keep their dark CRT surface where set with `!important` elsewhere.
  - Added attribute-selector overrides as a second safety net for inline `color:#fff` / `color:white` text and translucent-white panel backgrounds that become invisible on a white canvas.
- **New module — Morse Code Trainer** (📡, brain-cognitive category):
  - 3 difficulty tiers (A–Z / 0–9 / Mixed) + 3 modes (🔊 Listen → pick character, 👁️ See dits/dahs → pick character, 🔤 See character → pick code).
  - Audio playback synthesises real dits & dahs via Web Audio (sine 620 Hz, standard dot/dash = 1/3 unit timing, 18 WPM). 🔁 Replay button so kids/learners can hear it again.
  - 12-question round, score + streak HUD with lifetime totals in localStorage.
  - Collapsible Morse chart (📖) lists all 36 characters as a reference.
- **SW cache v57 → v58** to flush.
